title: Global generation is stalkwise surjectivity
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf
of $\Lambda_T$-modules on $T_{\Et}$, with evaluation morphism
$\bigoplus_{s\in\Gamma(T_{\Et},F)}\underline{\Lambda}\to F$ of
[def-kun-global-generated]. Then the following are equivalent:

1. **(1)** $F$ is globally generated, i.e. the evaluation morphism
is an epimorphism of sheaves;
1. **(2)** the evaluation morphism is surjective on every geometric
stalk of $T$.

proof.text: Let $e:E\to F$ be the evaluation morphism of [def-kun-global-generated], where $E=\bigoplus_{s\in\Gamma(T_{\Et},F)}\underline\Lambda$. Form its cokernel $C$ in the abelian category of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to the small etale site and $\mathcal O=\Lambda_T$: the functor $U$ forgetting scalars preserves cokernels, so $U(C)=\operatorname{coker}(U(e))$. Moreover $C$ is zero precisely when $U(C)$ is zero: in either case all section groups are trivial, and the unique maps to and from the zero sheaf are automatically linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero] in the module-sheaf category, $e$ is epic precisely when $C$ is zero. Thus global generation is equivalent to $U(C)=0$.

proof.text: For every geometric point $\bar t$, apply [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] to the abelian sheaf map $U(e)$. It identifies $U(C)_{\bar t}$ with the cokernel of $U(e)_{\bar t}$. Explicitly, a stalk element of a module sheaf $M$ is a germ $[V,\bar v,a]$ with $a\in M(V)$; two representatives are equal when their restrictions agree on a common pointed refinement, as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Forgetting scalars leaves these representatives and this equality relation unchanged. Addition is addition of restrictions on a common refinement, and $\lambda[V,\bar v,a]=[V,\bar v,\lambda a]$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$. The map on germs sends $[V,\bar v,a]$ to $[V,\bar v,e_V(a)]$ before and after forgetting scalars; hence the underlying group map of $e_{\bar t}$ is $U(e)_{\bar t}$. A homomorphism of modules is surjective precisely when its underlying group homomorphism is surjective; its group cokernel is the quotient by its image and is zero precisely in that case. Consequently $e_{\bar t}$ is surjective if and only if $U(C)_{\bar t}=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the morphism $U(C)\to0$ of abelian etale sheaves. The stalk of the zero sheaf is zero (the colimit of the zero section groups), so this morphism is an isomorphism precisely when $U(C)_{\bar t}=0$ for every geometric point. Its being an isomorphism is precisely $U(C)=0$. Combining this with steps 1 and 2 proves both implications of the asserted equivalence.
